contract:
FOLD THIS SIGNAL (plain text, no em-dashes, under 150 words): the row below is a signal an estate captured. Answer three things only: (1) TRUE-TODAY: is this signal still true given everything else you know in the row's context - yes/no/unknown with one line of why; (2) THE ORGAN: which kind of organ should own this signal (a law, a clock, a gate, a memory row, or compost); (3) THE FALSIFIER: the observation that would prove the signal wrong. Mark unknowns UNKNOWN; do not pad.

SIGNAL: CONTEXT: Two work paths P and H drain via N leaderless agents; split q = n_P/n_H is agent counts; backlogs B_P, B_H are counter-derived only (queued + unacked, decremented on commit, incremented on arrival). Goal implied by "co-termination": both paths finish at the same time, so no agent idles waiting on the other path. The split must be computed from measurements, never from a plan. ROLE: Control-loop designer for a self-allocating swarm; you produce one buildable mechanism, not a survey. TASK: Specify the mechanism that makes both backlogs hit zero simultaneously by driving the agent split
